sources.title: Calc Guide, Chapter 9: Using Formulas and Functions
Calc Guide, Chapter 2: Entering, Editing, and Formatting Data

notes.summary: Both Excel and Calc use formulas that begin with an equals sign. In Calc, enter the formula in a cell or the input line of the Formula Bar, then confirm it.
Calc's Function Wizard can help find a function and enter its arguments; use it when an Excel function name or syntax is unfamiliar.
In Calc, select a cell and type to enter data, then press Enter. To edit existing cell contents, press F2 or edit the input line on the Formula Bar, then confirm the change.
Excel formulas begin with an equals sign and can include functions, cell references, constants, and operators. A formula can be entered in a cell and confirmed with Enter.
Formula argument separators in Calc can depend on locale and configuration. If a copied formula is rejected, check the local separator setting rather than assuming the formula itself is unsupported.
